thread:
maya: quick RFC follow-up re: fallback policy DSL + runtime contract. want to align on where rules live and minimal surface the runtime needs.

alex: +1. we need something expressible for per-customer overrides, global fallbacks, and 'quality preference' (prefer cheaper model vs prefer fidelity).

sam: can we keep runtime tiny? ideally runtime reads a compact policy blob and exposes hooks: decideFallback(requestMeta) -> route | null, and reportTelemetry(event).

rachel: tradeoff: putting too much logic in runtime (e.g. latency forecasting) bloats binary and forces feature parity across deployments. prefer control-plane DSL that compiles to simple predicates.

maya: propose this split: control-plane policy language (declarative) -> compiler -> binary decision table + prioritized fallback list + backoff parameters. runtime only evaluates table + enforces circuit thresholds.

alex: sounds good. what about long-running sessions with KV cache? if we switch model mid-session fallback must preserve session affinity for cache hits or rebuild gracefully.

sam: two modes: session-affinitive (pin to original backend until session end) and stateless per-request. policy can choose. default: session-affinitive for chat, stateless for single-shot.

rachel: observability: decision events must include reason code, matched rule id, model_variant_outcome, latency_budget_remaining, token_budget. we need these to debug regressions. ops-bot should surface top failure reason to #oncall.

ops-bot: NOTE: When a fallback occurs, a telemetry event is emitted: fallback.event.v1 {rule_id, reason, from_model, to_model, latency_ms, user_tier}.

maya: small example DSL snippet (very rough):

```
policy "canary-fallback-v1" {
  match customer_tier in (enterprise, internal)
  prefer fidelity when request.sequence_len > 512
  fallback_chain ["redwood-llama-13b-q8", "redwood-llama-7b-q4"]
  circuit { failures: 10, window_ms: 60000, cooloff_ms: 300000 }
  session_affinity: true
}
```

alex: would prefer explicit numeric thresholds rather than fuzzy words like "prefer fidelity". also add a soft-budget gate: max_extra_cost_ms_per_minute per-customer to limit expensive fallbacks.

sam: runtime contract sketch:

```
// decision API exposed by runtime
decision = decide(request_meta) // returns {route, reason, rule_id}
report(decision, metrics) // best-effort, non-blocking
```

maya: on backward compatibility: control plane should ship compiler that emits both v1 and v0 artifacts for older runtimes for 3 months.

rachel: rollout plan: start with internal customers, watch fallback.rate and quality.regressions, then open to enterprise. add canary flag per-customer so we can toggle policy without redeploy.

alex: failure modes: 1) bad rule accidentally routes all traffic to cheap model -> need kill-switch on control-plane and runtime-level global guard (fail-closed to last-known-good). 2) telemetry loss -> we must degrade to conservative routing.

maya: decision: implement control-plane DSL + compiler. runtime changes: add tiny evaluate-table engine, expose decide/report API, implement session_affinity toggle, and global kill-switch. include telemetry schema defined by Rachel.

rachel: +1. I'll write telemetry schema PR and a short eval harness to simulate fallback churn vs cost savings.

sam: i'll prototype the runtime evaluate-table and the per-customer budget gate.

alex: ops: add runbook snippets for "unexpected mass fallback" and an emergency policy that routes 100% to golden model.

maya: action items: rachel => telemetry schema & runbook (due EOD Thu), sam => runtime prototype (Weds), alex => emergency policy + control-plane kill-switch (Mon), maya => DSL v1 spec draft (Fri).

deploy-bot: deploy started for infra/telemetry-schema PR #482

maya: thanks all, we'll sync in tomorrow's eng-platform sync. :thumbsup:
